data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible without smuggling in induction if reinterpreted as a methodological rule for selecting the most informative surviving conjecture for further testing, rather than as an inductive inference of future reliability; however, accepting this defense costs the scientist any rational guarantee that the chosen theory will succeed in practical application, forcing a leap of faith distinct from scientific rationality.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If one insists that 'preference for action' logically entails an expectation of future success derived from past success, then induction is smuggled in.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the Tich\u00fd/Miller proof against verisimilitude holds, then 'best-tested' cannot even be coherently defined as 'closest to truth,' undermining the selection criterion.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Popper's own advice to act on the best-tested theory implies he believed it was more reliable, then his philosophical distinction collapses in practice.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'scientific rationality' (choosing the theory with highest empirical content that has not yet been falsified, to maximize learning potential) and 'pragmatic action' (where no scientific rationality applies). The preference is not based on the probability of truth (which Popper rejects) but on the severity of tests passed, which indicates high informational content. When acting (e.g., building a bridge), the scientist steps outside the logical bounds of science proper and makes a non-rational, volitional commitment to the best-tested theory, acknowledging that this action cannot be justified by past performance alone.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
